flows.narrative: Despite the week's brutal price action (S&P down five straight sessions into Friday's sharpest single-day move), BOTH BofA/EPFR and Lipper's newly-published week-ended-18-Nov editions show net equity INFLOWS, not capitulation outflows -- a genuinely counterintuitive result this run flags rather than forces into the price/sentiment narrative. BofA/EPFR: global equity funds +$66.6bn, US equities +$45.6bn (7th straight week), tech funds +$5.4bn (8th straight week), EM equities +$8.3bn (8th straight week); bonds -$7.4bn (first outflow since April 2025) and EM debt -$7.5bn (most since April 2020); crypto funds -$1.1bn; BofA's own Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.1 from 7.4 (re-confirmed this run via an independent Yahoo Finance writeup of the same Hartnett note -- money-market +$0.4bn and gold +$0.2bn both matched exactly, cross-validating Saturday's bake rather than contradicting it).
